reasons.realCost: The bill can run several times the plan sticker once marketing contacts, extra seats, and the SMS add-on stack up, and Professional or Enterprise also carries a mandatory one-time onboarding fee of $3,000 or $7,000 on top of the subscription.
reasons.pricingHonesty: HubSpot publishes a full Product & Services Catalog with per-seat prices, contact-tier rates, and add-on costs, and its public price calculator shows a first-year total, onboarding included, before any sales call.
reasons.smallTeamFit: The free tools and Starter plan are simple to self-serve, but Starter caps email automation at 10 automated actions, so reaching multi-step automation pushes a team into Professional's required onboarding and 12-month commitment.
reasons.doesTheJob: Marketing Hub runs on the same Smart CRM database as HubSpot's sales, service, content, and data hubs, letting a business consolidate several functions under one shared contact record.
reasons.freedomToLeave: Starter can be paid and cancelled month to month, but Professional requires a 12-month commitment with no cancellation or downgrade mid-term and prepaid fees are non-refundable.
reasons.trackRecord: HubSpot has been publicly traded since 2014 and publishes a full product catalog, though its 2024 move to seat-based pricing changed how new customers pay for users.

basis: HubSpot's free tier and Starter plan are genuinely useful and honestly priced for a very small business, but growing past Starter's automation limits brings a mandatory onboarding fee, a 12-month lock-in, and a bill that can multiply well beyond the plan sticker once contacts, seats, and SMS are added.
method: Two independent blind passes scored six factors (1–5) and an overall; published overall is the lower of the two overall scores, because this tool runs an affiliate program we have joined or may join. Pass scores: 3.6 and 3.3.
